skill.name: faceless-explainer
skill.description: Create faceless explainer videos from text using HyperFrames, invented visuals, narration, captions, transitions, and final render checks.
skill.summary: Turn articles, notes, or briefs into faceless explainer videos with story, motion, audio, captions, and render steps.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown code spans, JavaScript template literals, regex .exec calls, and fixed sibling reference paths. Confirmed risks are intended local command execution, an environment-selected media engine, credential-dependent HeyGen audio retrieval, and a CDN dependency for GSAP. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: External command execution in the workflow
remediation.suggestion: Document every command that may run and require explicit user confirmation before commands update global tools or render projects.

remediation.issue: HF_MEDIA_ENGINE can select the executed media engine
remediation.suggestion: Validate HF_MEDIA_ENGINE against trusted paths or require an explicit command-line flag before executing an alternate engine.

remediation.issue: HeyGen credential and external audio processing dependency
remediation.suggestion: Document what content is sent to HeyGen services and ensure auth status output never includes tokens or secret values.

remediation.issue: External CDN dependency in generated HTML
remediation.suggestion: Bundle GSAP locally when possible, or keep SRI and crossorigin attributes and disclose the network requirement.

remediation.issue: Project scripts accept writable output paths
remediation.suggestion: Warn before writing outside the selected HyperFrames project root and prefer project-relative output paths.

content.value_statement: Text briefs often need a clear visual story before they can become useful videos. This skill turns source text into a HyperFrames explainer workflow.
actual_capabilities: Creates a HyperFrames project structure for a text-based explainer.
Guides storyboard and narration planning for concepts, how-tos, listicles, and story explainers.
Applies a frame preset and remixes brand colors or fonts when tokens exist.
Runs audio, caption, assembly, transition, lint, validation, preview, and render steps.
Builds invented visuals such as typography, diagrams, abstract graphics, and data visualizations.
limitations: Requires the HyperFrames CLI, Node scripts, and local project file access.
Not intended for product promos, website tours, PR videos, or existing footage captions.
HeyGen audio and media retrieval may require existing credentials or an offline fallback.
External commands and local file writes should be reviewed before use.

best_practices: Provide the source text, target audience, desired length, aspect ratio, and tone before starting.
Approve the frame-by-frame storyboard before audio generation or frame production begins.
Use real user-supplied assets only when they are needed and placed in the expected project paths.
anti_patterns: Using this skill for a product launch, website tour, pull request video, or existing footage captioning task.
Skipping the storyboard approval gate and moving directly to frame generation.
Requesting unrelated shell commands or broad filesystem inspection outside the video workflow.

faq.question: What does faceless mean here?
faq.answer: The video uses invented visuals like type, diagrams, abstract graphics, and data visuals instead of a filmed presenter.

faq.question: Can it use my article or notes?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow saves the source text and reshapes it into a storyboard and narration.

faq.question: Does it capture websites?
faq.answer: No. Website tours should use a website-to-video workflow instead.

faq.question: Does it need HeyGen credentials?
faq.answer: Some audio and media retrieval features may use HeyGen credentials. The workflow can continue offline when configured.

faq.question: What files does it produce?
faq.answer: It produces storyboard, script, frame HTML, captions, an assembled index, and a rendered MP4 when checks pass.
